chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from al-ʿAbbās ibn Maʿrūf, from ʿAlī ibn Mahziyār, from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from Ḥarīz ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Zurārah, who said:

I said to Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام: What statement suffices in the tashahhud in the first two rakʿahs? He said: That you say: I bear witness that there is no god but Allah alone, having no partner. I said: Then what suffices of the tashahhud in the last two rakʿahs? He said: The two testimonies.

key_terms.أَشْهَدُ: I bear witness; the formula of testimony
key_terms.التَّشَهُّدِ: the testimony recited in salat while sitting
key_terms.الرَّكْعَتَيْنِ الْآخِرَتَيْنِ: the final two units of the prayer
key_terms.الرَّكْعَتَيْنِ الْأَوَّلَتَيْنِ: the first two units of the prayer
key_terms.الشَّهَادَتَانِ: the two testimonies recited in tashahhud
key_terms.لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ: the declaration of tawhid affirming that none is worthy of worship but Allah
key_terms.وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ: alone, with no partner; emphasis on exclusive divine unity

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum tashahhud that suffices in the prayer according to Imam al-Baqir عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the minimum wording that suffices for the tashahhud in salat. Imam Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام states that in the first two rakʿahs, saying the testimony of tawhid is sufficient, and in the final two rakʿahs, the two testimonies suffice.
